items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: And that’s why I spent time with him when we’re around, I go up to his apartment and we hang.

ctx.x: really. And everybody is rushing to get — now they’re able to make their own CDs. And I was talking with some of the people from WBGO-FM in Newark. And they were saying that every week they get flooded with CDs from people they never even heard of. And they put on some of them and they are terrible. But what can you do? People have access to make them. And I think that the albums I’ve made I put a lot of thought into. And this is one of the things I admired about Herbie Hancock when he started doing his thing.…

lot of these young people now. They’re saying, and I’m applauding and I’m very much supportive of a lot of the things that Wynton Marsalis is doing and accomplishing. He’s been anointed in a special role now. And I’ve known him since he was a little boy because I knew his mother and father and I was at his house when he was just a little whippersnapper going around. Because I was working in New Orleans at the Royal Sonesta Hotel with the Newport All-Stars. And Ellis had myself and Lenny McBrowne, the drummer, to…
Man, you have given me some great food for thought today.
